title: The Fourteenth Ad Read
description: AG1 buys host-read podcast ads at scale. Reporting cited in the case-study sources puts spend at roughly $2.2M per month across shows including Huberman Lab and Rich Roll, with the host reading the spot in their own voice and describing their own morning use. Each host has a personal promo code and a dedicated landing page, and affiliate commissions of 20 to 50 percent are reported. The code and landing page let AG1 attribute each new customer to the specific host who sent them. Sources: Huberman Lab sponsors page; Wharton and Behind the Brand case studies.

title: Rest has a dress code
description: Oura released a Gucci edition of the ring priced at $950. The New York Times reported that the Gucci edition sold out while the standard ring had a waitlist. Oura's own launch post frames the collaboration as a fashion object: editorial still-life photography, velvet and textile styling, and lifestyle imagery rather than sleep or performance data. Sources: Oura blog, Introducing Gucci x Oura; New York Times coverage of the launch.

title: Center of the Ring
description: PRIME signed a global partnership with WWE that put its logo at the center of the WrestleMania ring mat. WWE described it as the first brand ever placed on the mat. PRIME also holds a global marketing partnership with UFC in which both corners of the Octagon are branded as PRIME Hydration Recovery Zones. Both deals are announced on the leagues' own sites. Sources: WWE.com partnership announcement; UFC.com partnership announcement.

title: Target-Exclusive, Pop-Tarts Flavored
description: PRIME and Pop-Tarts released a co-branded Ultra-Filtered protein shake with 32g of protein per bottle, in Frosted Strawberry and Frosted Chocolate Fudge. The product is sold exclusively at Target. Sources: Yahoo Lifestyle coverage of the launch; Stack3d product write-up.

title: The First Redesign in a Decade
description: In 2024 Liquid I.V. changed its packaging for the first time in over a decade: a new hexagonal logo, heavier typography, and fruit illustration on the front of the packet in place of the earlier clinical-style layout. The company's release describes the goal as standing out on shelf. It is the brand's first visual identity change since Unilever acquired it in 2020. Sources: PR Newswire release; FoodNavigator coverage.

title: Fuel Your Play
description: Fuel Your Play was Liquid I.V.'s first out-of-home advertising campaign, reported at $20M in spend. Placements included golf courses, transit, and a 3D billboard. The company reported more than 40 million impressions in the campaign's first six weeks. The stated message was that hydration products are for everyday activity, not only athletes. Source: Marketing Dive, Campaign Trail.

title: LIVE.FIT.GO.™
description: LIVE. FIT. GO. is Celsius's first formal brand platform, developed with the agency Anomaly. The company describes it as the largest campaign in its history. The campaign positions the drink as fuel for everyday activity and runs the same message across settings, including gym and leisure contexts. Source: Celsius Holdings investor release announcing the campaign.

title: The Breakaway Sponsorship
description: Celsius signed a multi-year deal as presenting sponsor of all 10 Breakaway Music Festival stops. The sponsored run is branded the Essential Vibes Tour, putting the Celsius name on the festival itself rather than on a single booth or ad. Source: BevNET coverage of the sponsorship announcement.

title: The Box That Arrived Before You Slept
description: AG1 Pro ships with a printed data sheet inside the box citing results from four placebo-controlled randomized clinical trials. The trials were announced alongside the product's release. The box is the first physical contact most direct-order customers have with the product, so the trial summary reaches them before any store display would. Source: PR Newswire release on the AG1 Pro launch and trial results.

title: Pumpkin Spice Latte Season
description: The Pumpkin Spice Latte was introduced in 2003 and returns each year in late August, before the calendar start of fall. Its return date is announced in advance and covered annually as a seasonal marker. Source: TheStreet coverage of the 2026 fall menu.

title: A Cafe Where the Cereal Used to Be
description: Starbucks operates licensed counters inside grocery stores, run by the grocer under the Starbucks name. Separately, a pink Starbucks x Stanley Quencher tumbler sold exclusively at Target sold out within minutes of release, and listings reached about $400 on eBay. Both are retail placements outside Starbucks's own cafes. Sources: TODAY and NBC News coverage of the Stanley cup sellout.

title: The Membership Behind the Jewelry
description: The Oura Ring costs $349 to $499 up front. Full readiness, sleep, and stress detail requires an Oura membership at $5.99 per month. The CEO has said the fee funds continuous software updates. In 2026, lawsuits filed against the company allege the membership requirement amounts to a bait-and-switch on a device marketed as a premium purchase; those claims are allegations and have not been decided. Source: Yahoo Finance interview with the Oura CEO on the membership model.

title: WHOOP 5.0 & MG
description: In May 2025 WHOOP announced WHOOP 5.0 and WHOOP MG. The new band is 7 percent smaller than the prior generation and samples sensors 26 times per second. The launch introduced Healthspan and, on the MG hardware, Blood Pressure Insights. WHOOP's launch material describes the MG tier as medical-grade rather than fitness-tracker grade; that description is the company's own framing. Source: Tom's Guide launch coverage.

title: The Best Obsess
description: WHOOP's campaign The Best Obsess features Michael Phelps, Alex Honnold, and Virgil van Dijk on camera saying they are obsessed. The campaign presents obsession as part of elite performance rather than a flaw. WHOOP has stated that Phelps wore the device before any commercial agreement existed. Source: Athletech News coverage of the campaign.

title: Grab Life By the Claw
description: Teddy Swims fronts the second year of White Claw's Grab Life By The Claw campaign. The partnership includes tour sponsorship, an acoustic performance, and a television spot in which his band's rehearsal in an empty villa turns into a house party. Source: PR Newswire release on the White Claw and Teddy Swims partnership.

title: The Wave
description: White Claw's Wave display is a sculptural in-store stacker built entirely from the brand's own case art, sized to stand well above a standard aisle. The same display format has been relocated from retail stores to festival entrances, where it functions as a landmark rather than a point of sale. Source: PopIn case study, Surf's Up for White Claw Stacker Display.

title: Holding the Tin Up Like It's Sacred
description: A common ZYN meme format shows someone holding a tin up toward the camera, presenting it rather than opening it. The gesture reflects an existing user behavior of showing the tin to a room or a group chat before use. The format circulates through user-made content; no company ad uses it. Source: Nicotine Pouch ZYN Memes roundup.

title: The Tin Collection as Home Decor
description: Some users keep empty ZYN tins and display them instead of throwing them out. One documented example on Wikimedia Commons is a Christmas tree assembled from stacked tins. The behavior is user-originated and is not part of any company campaign. Claims about other tin sculptures are anecdotal and not sourced here. Source: Wikimedia Commons, Zyn_christmas_tree.jpg.
